Vimal Kumar Yadav Principal District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Fsat No. 05/2023 Cnr No. Dlnd01-002525-2023 1. Sh. Mahesh Malik S/o. Sh. S.L. Malik M/s. Malik Brothers, 44, Defence Colony Market, New Delhi-110024. R/o. A-360, Defence Colony, New Delhi-110024. 2. Sh. Harish Malik S/o. Sh. Sunder Lal Malik M/s. Malik Brothers, 44, Defence Colony Market, New Delhi-110024. R/o. A-360, Defence Colony, New Delhi-110024. 3. M/s. Malik Brothers 44, Defence Colony Market, New Delhi-110 024. Through Mahesh Malik, partner/Authorized Signatory ........ Appellants Versus State Through Ms. Chittra Bamola Food Safety Officer, Department of Food Safety, Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Place, New Delhi-110001. ....... Respondent Date of Institution : 10.03.20 Date of hearing arguments : 09.07.20 Date of Judgment : 22.07.20 Appearances: Sh. Satish Solanki and Ms. Samiksha, Ld. Counsels for the appellants. Sh. Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State/Respondent. Fsat No.05/2023 Sh.Mahesh Malik & Ors.Vs. State through Ms. Chittra Bamola, Fso, Delhi Judgment 1. The Appellant preferred an appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (as amended upto Mahesh Malik And Others vs State Through Fso on 22 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175803281/ 1 date) hereinafter referred to as 'The Act' assailing the order No. 146/Adm(Se)/Fs Cases/2022/9987-91 dated 01.02.2023 passed by Sh. Shailendra Kumar Singh, Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate, South-East District, New Delhi, whereby penalty of Rs.50,000/- each (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) was imposed on appellant No.1 being Food Business Operator (FBO)-cum-Partner and appellant No.2 being nominee of accused No.3 and a further penalty of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) was imposed upon Appellant No. 3, in terms of Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with directions that said penalty should be deposited within three (03) weeks of the receipt the order in the form of a Crossed Demand Draft drawn on a Nationalized Bank in favour of Adjudicating Officer, District South East, payable at Delhi. Brief Facts 2.
texts.facts: The Appellant preferred an appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (as amended upto Mahesh Malik And Others vs State Through Fso on 22 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175803281/ 1 date) hereinafter referred to as 'The Act' assailing the order No. 146/Adm(Se)/Fs Cases/2022/9987-91 dated 01.02.2023 passed by Sh. Shailendra Kumar Singh, Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate, South-East District, New Delhi, whereby penalty of Rs.50,000/- each (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) was imposed on appellant No.1 being Food Business Operator (FBO)-cum-Partner and appellant No.2 being nominee of accused No.3 and a further penalty of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) was imposed upon Appellant No. 3, in terms of Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with directions that said penalty should be deposited within three (03) weeks of the receipt the order in the form of a Crossed Demand Draft drawn on a Nationalized Bank in favour of Adjudicating Officer, District South East, payable at Delhi. Brief Facts 2. It is stated that on 12.08.2021, at about 06.31 pm, a sample of "Almonds" in sealed packs of 250 grams was lifted by Ms. Chittra Bamola, Food Safety Officer, for its analysis under the provisions of the Act from Sh. Mahesh Malik, FBO-cum- Partner (Appellant No.1) at M/s. Malik Brothers (Appellant No.3) from their outlet at 44, Defence Colony Market, New Delhi. The sample was divided into four equal parts, fastened and sealed according to rules and regulations and signed by FBO and the same was sent to the Food Analyst, GNCTD for analysis on 13.08.2021. The food Analyst analyzed the sample and reported the sample to be misbranded because there was violation of 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 & 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011. Thereafter, the appellant was provided an opportunity to file an appeal u/s 46 (4) of FSS Act, however, no appeal was preferred by the appellants against the report of the Food Analyst. Thereafter, Ld. Adjudicating Officer after going through the documents available on record found the appellant guilty for selling 'Misbranded Food Article' in violation of Section 23 (1), 26 (2) (ii), 27 (1), 27 (3) (c) read with Section 3 (1) (zf) of the FSS Act r/w Regulation No. 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 & 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P & L) Regulation, thereby imposing a penalty of Rs. 50,000/- each upon R-1 and R-2 and penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/- upon R-3. GROUNDS OF APPEAL 3. The appellants have assailed the impugned order passed by the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate on the ground that it has been passed hurriedly without appreciating that the sampled commodity was not meant for sale to the consumers at large but were being packed as per customer's order. It is further asserted that on analysis, the said sample was declared to be misbranded by the Food Analyst vide its report dated 26.08.2021 on the ground that the label of sample was without declaration of FSSAI Logo, Licence Number, name of food, vegetarian symbol, name and complete address of manufacturer, net quantity, batch number, date of packing and best before date and, therefore, the sample contravened Sections 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011. The sampled commodity was otherwise found conforming to the quality characteristics/parameters as prescribed under the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products Standards & Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, as reflected in Food Analyst's report dated 26.05.2021 ARGUMENTS Mahesh Malik And Others vs State Through Fso on 22 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175803281/ 2 4.
texts.arguments: It is pertinent to mention here that the appellants had already accepted their guilt before the Adjudicating Authority thus, the scope of appeal becomes limited, especially when it is not contended that the plea of guilt was not voluntary. 5. Notwithstanding the grounds of appeal taken, the counsel for the appellant has submitted, rather admitted, that the sampled product was to be labeled and stickers were to be pasted on the plastic packet but before it could be done, the sample was lifted. It is further submitted that the Almonds were otherwise found to be conforming to the norms and requirements of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Thus, in these circumstances, punishment awarded by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM is excessive, disproportionate and exorbitant. 6. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulations, 2011 are primarily, if not entirely, concerned with the quality of the food and if it is found that it is free from adulteration of any nature, then the primary purpose of the food item stands achieved. The labeling and branding, etc are secondary aspect of the food safety measures. In addition to the aforesaid contention, it has also been mentioned in the appeal that appellant No.3 is a partnership firm and Harish Malik was appointed Nominee under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, therefore, appellant No.1 Mahesh Malik was not responsible in any manner for the conduct of the business of appellant No.3. Accordingly, there could not have been any punishment/penalty for appellant No.1. 7. It is further asserted on behalf of the appellant that the request for taking a lenient view was, apparently, declined by the Adjudicating Officer/ADM whereas the case of the appellant was a fit case where indulgence should have been given by the Adjudicating Authority in view of the fact that food product "Almonds" were free from any kind of adulteration, etc and conformed to the norms provided under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The penalty imposed, it is submitted, is therefore arbitrary and harsh and is required to be waived off. 8. It is submitted that there is no independent witness for sampling and preparation of the documents related to the sampling which in itself is a ground to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order. An opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses was not given to the appellant, therefore, the impugned order deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK], through which the partnership firm, appellant No.3 and appellant No.1 and 2 i.e. Mahesh Malik and Harish Malik respectively have been imposed with a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) on the partnership firm and Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each on the FBO, Nominee and the one found at the spot selling the 'Almonds' respectively. 9. The Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State/Respondent, on the other hand, contended that the requirements of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the Regulations therein are required to be adhered to and there cannot be any pick and choose, as has been suggested by the appellant. If misbranding is an offence, then in the case of misbranding, statutory punishment is Mahesh Malik And Others vs State Through Fso on 22 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175803281/ 3 required to be considered and awarded to the persons violating the laws, notwithstanding the fact that there was no flaw either in the quantity or quality of the product i.e. "Almond".
